outcomes: View their life within the broader society in which they live. This provides a more global and multicultural perspective.
Students will understand the critical role social factors play in determining the health of individuals, groups, and the larger society.
Students will have increased critical thinking skills that will enable them to analyze, evaluate, and make decisions concerning complex contemporary social issues.
Students will be able to evaluate the impact of culture, social class, sex, race/ethnicity, and age on people’s life chances, practices, and attitudes.
Understand how their own culture and socialization, along with social inequality and institutions, have influenced their personal lives.
Demonstrate an understanding of the perspectives, methods and core concepts of sociology.
Demonstrate an understanding of and ability to describe the contribution and perspectives of women, ethnic and other minorities, and Western and non-Western peoples.
Explain the major problems and issues in the disciplines in their contemporary, historical, and geographical contexts.
